thread.title: Stocks Climb Ahead Of Apple; This Dow Stock Soars | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Climb Ahead Of Apple; This Dow Stock Soars | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks jumped to early gains Thursday in November's first trading session, as the market looked to extend its two-day rally attempt.
X Dow stock DowDupont ( DWDP ) spiked after its third-quarter report. Oil producer Newfield Exploration ( NFX ) also jumped on earnings and merger news.
Among the big tech names, Apple ( AAPL ) edged up 0.5% ahead of its earnings report, due after the close . Netflix ( NFLX ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) were both poised for strong starts. Chip stocks were mixed as NXP Semiconductors ( NXP ) and Qorvo ( QRVO ) climbed, and Veeco Instruments ( VECO ) took a deep dive after reporting results.
The Dow Jones industrial average led the early advance, up 0.5%. The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 each climbed 0.4%.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Parts of the market kept to a holding pattern, with Apple's earnings due out after today's close and October payrolls data set for release before Friday's open. Wednesday was the second day of a rally attempt. It's best to see a follow-through day occur on the fourth day or later of a rally attempt, but a powerful rally in higher volume on Thursday could be enough to kick the market out of its correction .
Job Cuts Soar, Productivity Slows, Oil Prices Slip U.S. productivity rose 2.2% in the third quarter, according to preliminary estimates from the Labor Department. That was down from a 3% rise in the second quarter, and just shy of economist estimates for a 2.3% gain. But it marked the best consecutive quarters' growth in nearly three years. Unit labor costs gained 1.2%, reversing a 1% decline from the second quarter, and outpacing estimates for a 1.1% increase.
Challenger, Grey & Christmas said layoffs rose 37% in October, to 75,644. The number was up 153% from year-ago levels, and the highest since July 2015.
First-time unemployment applications showed little change, down a fraction to 214,000 in the week ended Oct. 27. Economists had projected a decrease to 212,000 claims.
Manufacturing purchasing managers indexes and September construction spending figures are scheduled later this morning. Automakers are due to report October sales results throughout the day.
Oil prices made a significant move Wednesday, as West Texas Intermediate dropped 1.3% to $65.31 a barrel. That ended a struggle to retake technical support at its 200-day moving average. On Thursday, WTI trimmed its early loss to trade flat just above $65 a barrel, a psychological level of support. Earlier, oil dropped below $65 for its third time since June. Prices declined 10.8% in October, oil's worst month since July 2016.
Global Markets: Hong Kong Surges, Europe Weakens In China, Hong Kong's market picked up on Wednesday's U.S. tech rally, sending the Hang Seng Index up 1.8%. China's top policy-making body said Wednesday that the economy was under "growing downward pressure," but that the Politburo would stimulate the market and capital markets. The Shanghai Composite edged up 0.1%.
Traders in Japan, however, focused on the "downward pressure" portion of the Politburo's statement, sending Tokyo's Nikkei 225 down 1.1%.
In Europe, stocks abruptly narrowed early losses after the Bank of England held its interest rate target steady, but lowered its growth and inflation forecast, and signaled a faster pace of rate hikes. Frankfurt's DAX halved its early gain to 0.4%, while London's FTSE 100 fought to a 0.2% gain and the CAC-40 in Paris dipped into narrow losses.
FANG Stocks Lean Higher; DowDupont Spikes Netflix opened up 1% and Amazon added 1.8%. A 5.6% bounce on Wednesday left Netflix on positive ground for the week, but still 4% below a test of resistance at its 10-week moving average. The stock dropped 19% in October, leaving it down 29% from a June high, aiming to start up the right side of the four-month consolidation.
Amazon popped 4.4% on Wednesday, but remained down 2.7% for the week and working on its fifth straight weekly decline. The stock dropped 20% in October, Amazon's worst month since Nov. 2008. Shares remain below their 40-week moving average, and about 20% below their September high.
DowDupont powered up 7.2%, after reporting a 35% earnings gain and a 31% rise in revenue for its third quarter. Revenue was just a shade below expectations, but the company announced a $3 billions stock buyback program and raised its cost synergies target to $3.6 billion. DowDuPont shares have rebounded over the past three sessions, trimming the stock's loss for October to 16%.
Chipmarket NXP Jumps; Encana Buys Newfield Among chipmakers, NXP Semiconductors cut loose a 9.1% advance after reporting results. The Netherlands-based chip maker is deep in an eight-month correction.
Qorvo bolted 5% higher after reporting above-forecast fiscal second-quarter earnings, although its third-quarter guidance missed analysts' targets. The gain sent shares back above their 10-week moving average, to a test of resistance at their 40-week line.
Veeco Instruments crumbled 19% at the start of trade. The Plainview, N.Y.-based chip-equipment maker reported mixed third-quarter earnings, and announced it had discovered an attack on its computer systems. Management said law enforcement had been notified, and forensic experts had been hired. The announcement said the attack and related expenses could a have material impact on the company's operating results and financial condition. Veeco shares are now 78% below a July 2017 high.
Newfield Exploration swept 13.6% higher, after Canadian oil name Encana ( ECA ) said it would acquire the outfit in a deal valued near $5.5 billion, including $2.2 billion in debt. Encana shares dropped 14.8%, on the takeover news and following its third-quarter results.
Apache slipped 1.5% in early trade. The international oil play reported a 1,475% surge in third-quarter earnings and a 26% revenue gain. The company raised its fourth-quarter production guidance, and said full-year production would come in near the top of the forecast range.
